n: Right after the Exodus, the Lord gives Moses instructions about Israel’s firstborn.
Every firstborn male, human and animal, belongs to the Lord. Having spared Israel’s firstborn, God claims them as His own.
Moses tells the people to remember this day of release from “the house of bondage,” accomplished by the Lord’s mighty hand.
They left in the month of Abib, meaning “fresh ears of grain”—springtime.

f.g: “young ears of grain”; later called Nisan

n: Once in the promised land, they must keep this observance every year in this month.
Seven days of unleavened bread end with a festival on the seventh day.
No yeast was to be seen anywhere in their territory during the feast.
Parents were to explain to their children: we do this because of what the Lord did for me. Each generation was to see the Exodus as personal.

f.w: that which the LORD did unto me

n: The feast would serve as a reminder, as if on their hand and forehead, keeping God’s law in their mouths. Later Jews literally wore small scripture boxes (tefillin) based on verses like this.

f.w: a sign unto thee upon thine hand

n: This ordinance must be kept at its appointed time every year.
When the Lord gives them Canaan as promised, they must observe the law of the firstborn.
All firstborn males—of people and livestock—were to be dedicated to the Lord.

A firstborn donkey, which couldn’t be sacrificed, was to be “redeemed” by substituting a lamb. Firstborn sons were always redeemed—bought back by an offering. The idea of a substitute points toward Christ.

f.g: buy back by paying a substitute

n: When children ask what this means, parents should tell of the Lord’s strong hand in delivering them from slavery.
Because the Lord struck Egypt’s firstborn when Pharaoh refused, Israel offers its firstborn animals and redeems its sons.

f.g: stubbornly refused to let us go

n: This would be a sign on the hand and “frontlets” between the eyes—an ever-present reminder.
God did not lead them along the short coastal road through Philistine territory, where they would face war and might turn back. God knows what we are ready for.

f.w: the way of the land of the Philistines
f.g: the main coastal road to Canaan, heavily guarded

n: Instead God led them the long way, by the wilderness road toward the Red Sea. They went out organized and ready.

f.g: in battle array, organized (perhaps “in groups of fifty”)

n: Moses took Joseph’s bones, fulfilling the oath Israel made to Joseph centuries earlier. God’s promises, and Israel’s, were kept.
They traveled from Succoth to Etham at the edge of the desert.

f.g: a site on the edge of the wilderness; exact location unknown

n: The Lord Himself led them in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night, giving guidance and light. Latter-day prophecy promises a similar divine presence over Zion.
The pillar never left them. God’s constant guidance was visible every day and every night.

f.w: He took not away the pillar
